note: Every entry here was found by direct live verification against a real running APEX 26.1 instance, not inferred from documentation. This is a structured index of facts already documented in prose across docs/grammar-assumptions.md and inline source comments -- see the 'source' field on each entry for the full story. This file is documentation, not (yet) wired into any runtime warning mechanism -- see docs/ecosystem-roadmap.md for why that's a deliberate scoping decision, not an oversight.

quirks.issue: getRecords() and getModel() throw a runtime error instead of returning data, even though both methods exist on the widget's method list.
quirks.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'each'), thrown from inside APEX's own modelViewBase.min.js. Confirmed twice: immediately after navigation, and again after an awaited refresh() -- not a timing fluke.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (faceted-search-cards page)
quirks.workaround: Use getPageInfo(), getSelectedRecords()/setSelectedRecords(), or a DOM locator (find a card by index or contained text) instead of getRecords()/getModel().
quirks.status: confirmed-broken

quirks.issue: Checking page.url() once immediately after waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded') is a race condition against an async/AJAX-driven login redirect -- the check can run before the URL actually changes, reporting failure on a login that actually succeeded.
quirks.evidence: A run that threw 'URL unchanged after submit' had its failure screenshot show the user already logged in on the real post-login dashboard. An earlier, wrong diagnosis ('Enter-key submission is unreliable, switch to a button click') was tried first and also failed the same way -- the bug was in success-detection timing, not the submission method.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample File Upload and Download app (second, independent APEX 26.1 app)
quirks.workaround: Wait for an actual URL change (page.waitForURL(url => url !== loginUrl, { timeout })) instead of a single point-in-time check after waitForLoadState.
quirks.status: fixed, fix not independently re-verified

quirks.issue: Playwright's toBeVisible()/toBeHidden() are unsafe against these elements. Even with the correct u-visible CSS class applied, the element's rendered height stayed exactly 0px when the message was triggered by calling apex.message.showPageSuccess()/showErrors() directly (bypassing a real form submission) -- confirmed stuck, not a transient animation, checked repeatedly over 1.8s.
quirks.evidence: getComputedStyle showed display:block, visibility:visible, opacity:1, height:0px simultaneously. Because the box is always zero-height in this app/theme, toBeHidden() would ALSO trivially pass even while a message genuinely is showing -- unsafe in both directions.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (data-entry-simple-form page)
quirks.workaround: Assert the u-visible/u-hidden CSS class directly (toHaveClass(/u-visible/)) instead of rendered visibility.
quirks.status: worked around, root cause (why height stays 0 under direct invocation) not diagnosed

quirks.issue: Search/sort/pagination internals are implemented as _-prefixed methods on the underlying widget instance (jQuery-UI-widget-factory convention) -- there is no public, documented way to drive them via a JS method call.
quirks.evidence: Enumerated the widget instance's full prototype method list live: only refresh, openDialogChat, openInlineChat, closeChat are public (non-underscore). Everything else (_search, _paginate, _reset, _download, ...) is private by convention. Separately, apex.region(id).call(action) -- the generic action-dispatch API -- was tested with a dozen plausible action names (refresh, search, getViews, getCurrentView, reset, collapse, ...) and rejected every one with "Call not supported."
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (browse-interactive-report page)
quirks.workaround: Use the generic ApexRegion methods (refresh, getViewName, getSessionState) for what they support. Drive search/sort/pagination through the actual UI (fill the visible search input, click column-header sort links) via Playwright locators -- not a JS API call. UPDATE (Eighth round, 2026-08-01): this is now IMPLEMENTED, not just a suggestion -- see packages/testkit/src/components/interactive-report.ts (searchInteractiveReport/sortReportColumn/getColumnSortState), confirmed live against the same app/page. See the new 'interactive-report-accessible-locator-search-sort' entry for the evidence. Pagination specifically remains unimplemented -- no live multi-page dataset was available to verify next/prev click behavior.
quirks.status: confirmed, permanent constraint (not a bug to fix, a real API boundary) -- UI-driven workaround now built and verified, see 'interactive-report-accessible-locator-search-sort'

quirks.issue: Calling fetchCounts() and immediately reading getTotalResourceCount() is unreliable -- the count can still return null. This holds even in a genuinely fresh Playwright browser context, not just a warmed/reused tab.
quirks.evidence: Discovered the real fix by monkey-patching $.fn.trigger to log every event actually fired during fetchCounts(): apexbeforerefresh then apexafterrefresh fire directly on the region's own DOM element once the async count-fetch completes.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (faceted-search-cards page)
quirks.workaround: Use fetchCountsAndWait() instead of fetchCounts() -- waits for the real apexafterrefresh event before resolving, verified reliable across 3 repeated live runs.
quirks.status: fixed and verified

quirks.component: APEX client lifecycle events (apexbeforerefresh, apexafterrefresh, and likely others)
quirks.issue: These are jQuery custom events, not native DOM CustomEvents. A plain element.addEventListener('apexafterrefresh', ...) never fires.
quirks.evidence: Confirmed live: only apex.jQuery(el).on()/.trigger() -- not addEventListener/dispatchEvent -- sees these events.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (faceted-search-cards page)
quirks.workaround: Always use apex.jQuery (Oracle's documented stable reference, not a bare global $/jQuery) to listen for these events, never native addEventListener.
quirks.status: confirmed, permanent constraint

quirks.component: Region identifiers -- universal mechanism, confirmed on Interactive Grid, Chart, AND Interactive Report
quirks.issue: The DOM/runtime id apex.region() resolves against does not always match the .apx declared region identifier. Originally confirmed on Interactive Grid (export "basic-editing" -> runtime "emp") and Chart (export "area-chart-color-javascript-code-customization" -> runtime "area1"). CORRECTED (same-day, later pass): this was believed narrower -- an earlier version of this entry claimed 'Interactive Report/Cards/Faceted Search regions have matched export id to runtime id in every app checked so far'. That claim was wrong, based on incomplete sampling. A real interactiveReport region (sample-charts, export identifier "projects") has advanced { htmlDomId: projects_report } -- confirmed live: apex.region('projects') -> false, apex.region('projects_report') -> true. htmlDomId is a UNIVERSAL region-level mechanism, not gated to Chart/Interactive Grid -- a full sweep of the 13-app local corpus found it set on 6/86 (~7%) of interactiveReport/cards/facetedSearch regions too (5 IR, 1 Cards, 0 Faceted Search in that sample).
quirks.evidence: Live, in authenticated sessions: apex.region('basic-editing') -> null, apex.region('emp') -> real region (Interactive Grid, Sample Interactive Grids app). apex.region('area-chart-color-javascript-code-customization') -> null, apex.region('area1') -> real region with widget container id 'area1_jet' (Chart, Sample Charts app). apex.region('projects') -> false, apex.region('projects_report') -> true (Interactive Report, Sample Charts app, page 13) -- confirmed the SAME htmlDomId mechanism, no widget-specific suffix needed for plain apex.region() resolution (unlike Chart/IG's OWN internal widget-factory dispatch, which additionally appends _jet/_ig to reach a nested widget container -- a separate, component-specific concern layered on top, not part of generic region resolution). Root cause: the .apx export's `region { advanced { htmlDomId: ... } } }` property, when present, deterministically IS the runtime id apex.region() resolves -- confirmed exactly on `pie-chart`->`pie1`, `donut-chart-sorting`->`donut1`, `bar-chart-stack-label-stack-category`->`stackCategoryChart`, `projects`->`projects_report` (Sample Charts app) and `basic-editing`->`emp` consistently across every Interactive Grid page in that export. When `htmlDomId` is absent (confirmed: 66/97 real chart regions in Sample Charts; ~93% of IR/Cards/Faceted Search regions in the local corpus), the export identifier itself is usually the runtime id (fallback, not a guarantee) -- except for the Chart subset specifically confirmed to have NO corresponding field anywhere in the static export at all (an APEX-internal auto-generated numeric id, e.g. `R738095923010136870`). This is now typed at the parser level as `ApexRegion.htmlDomId` (packages/parser/src/ast.ts).
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Interactive Grids (Basic Editing page); Sample Charts (Area, Bar, Pie, Interactive Report pages)
quirks.workaround: Read `ApexRegion.htmlDomId` from the parsed AST first, for ANY region type -- when non-null, that value IS the runtime static id apex.region() resolves directly (Chart/Interactive Grid additionally append _jet/_ig on top of this, for their own nested widget container, not for generic apex.region() resolution). When `htmlDomId` is null, the export identifier is the runtime id in the large majority of cases (~93% for IR/Cards/Faceted Search checked so far) but treat this as a fallback assumption, not a guarantee -- verify per instance where it matters, especially before auto-generating an assertion against it.
quirks.status: LIVE-confirmed on Interactive Grid, Chart, and Interactive Report; STATICALLY confirmed present (htmlDomId set in real export data, no live app available to verify actual runtime resolution) on map and classicReport too, via ujnak/APEXlang-exports (draw-polygon-on-map's `map` region, menu-popup-with-action/salary-management-agent's `classicReport` regions) -- root cause diagnosed for the live-confirmed cases; open for Cards/Faceted Search (0 confirmed instances with htmlDomId set yet, but not ruled out -- small sample) and for whether map/classicReport's static htmlDomId actually predicts the runtime id the same way, pending live access to an app that has one. **UPDATE (21-app addition, oracle/apex 26.1 branch + 3 independents, static-only -- no live access to any of these apps either)**: htmlDomId confirmed present in real export data on 22 MORE region types never checked for it before: staticContent, list, plugin/badgeList, themeTemplateComponent/contentRow, plSqlDynamicContent, regionDisplaySelector, themeTemplateComponent/comments, breadcrumb, dynamicContent, cards, facetedSearch, smartFilters, plugin/componentInstructions, search, reflowReport, columnToggleReport, themeTemplateComponent/avatar, themeTemplateComponent/mediaList, themeTemplateComponent/timeline, themeTemplateComponent/metricCard, themeTemplateComponent/flexboxContainer, plugin/html5BarChart, plugin/tagCloud -- plus a much richer static sample on `map` (11 of 18 real map regions in `sample-maps` have it set, vs. the single prior instance). Literal evidence, a representative sample: `sample-maps` region `us-airports` -> `advanced { htmlDomId: airport-map-region }`; `universal-theme-reference` region `demo` (classicReport) -> `advanced { htmlDomId: DemoA }` (the `reflowReport` instance); `customers` region `customer-summary-with-references-no-products` (plugin/badgeList) -> `advanced { htmlDomId: CUST_SUM_W_REFS_NO_PRODS }`. All 22 are static-only confirmation, consistent with (not contradicting) the 'universal mechanism' finding -- this is now confirmed on 27 total region types (5 previously + 22 this round), a substantial strengthening, not a new phenomenon.
quirks.source: packages/parser/src/ast.ts (ApexRegion.htmlDomId), packages/testkit/src/components/interactive-grid.ts, packages/testkit/src/components/chart.ts, packages/testkit/src/components/region.ts (expectRegionsResolve), .ai/ADR/003-region-resolution-layered-strategy.md, docs/grammar-assumptions.md, .ai/knowledge/verification.md (ujnak/APEXlang-exports, oracle/apex 26.1 branch, independent apps)

quirks.issue: A plain page.goto() to a friendly URL for a protected page -- even immediately after a successful, verified login, even to the EXACT page just landed on -- silently redirects to /login (HTTP 200, not an error) instead of loading the page. This holds regardless of whether a session= query parameter is included.
quirks.evidence: Live: right after login(), landed on .../home?session=<id> (real, authenticated, correct title). A subsequent page.goto('.../home') (bare, no click) redirected to /login. A subsequent page.goto('.../basic-editing') did the same, with and without an explicit ?session=<id> appended. A genuine in-app link CLICK (e.g. the Help top-nav link, or the Editing/Basic Editing card links) worked correctly every time and stayed authenticated. The app's application.apx / page .apx source declares `pageAccessProtection: argumentsMustHaveChecksum` -- APEX's own documented security feature requiring a valid, per-render checksum on requests to these pages, which a hand-typed or scripted goto() URL does not carry (only APEX's own rendered links do).
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Interactive Grids gallery app (Basic Editing page, page 30; also confirmed on Home, page 1)
quirks.workaround: For apps/pages with this protection enabled, navigate via real in-app link clicks (page.getByRole('link', ...).click()), not page.goto() to a friendly URL -- even for the generator's own gotoApexPage()-based page objects. This is a real, correctly-functioning APEX security feature, not a bug in this project's tooling -- but it means the generator's default navigation strategy (bare goto()) will not work against pages configured this way.
quirks.status: confirmed, root cause diagnosed

quirks.issue: Pages using a modal dialog page mode return HTTP 400 on a plain friendly-URL GET, instead of loading normally.
quirks.evidence: Confirmed live on p00420 (Data Entry -- Drawer Form) -- 4 generated tests fail this way, consistently, out of 43 total.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (p00420-data-entry-drawer-form)
quirks.workaround: None yet -- these pages likely need a parent-page/dialog-opening context that neither the generator nor gotoApexPage constructs today.
quirks.status: confirmed, root cause not diagnosed

quirks.issue: Interactive Grid is NOT driven the same way as Interactive Report/Cards. Its methods live behind a jQuery UI widget-factory call (apex.region(id).widget().interactiveGrid(method)), not directly on the apex.region(id) object the way region.ts's generic ApexRegion methods are for IR/Cards. Confirmed working via that path: getActions, getViews, getCurrentView, getCurrentViewId, getSelectedRecords. Confirmed REJECTED with a clear "no such method" error (not a silent failure): model, view, getRegion.
quirks.evidence: Live, method-by-method: interactiveGrid('getActions') returned a real apex.actions instance ({add, remove, invoke, toggle, list, ...}); interactiveGrid('getViews') returned {grid, chart}; interactiveGrid('getCurrentViewId') returned a string; interactiveGrid('getCurrentView') returned a rich view controller object (getSelectedRecords/setSelectedRecords/getActiveRecordId/gotoCell observed as properties on it, not yet individually invoked and confirmed); interactiveGrid('getSelectedRecords') called directly also succeeded. interactiveGrid('model'/'view'/'getRegion') all threw "no such method '<name>' for interactiveGrid widget instance". Separately: apex.region(id).call('refresh'|'getSelectedRecords'|'getActions') ALSO succeeded for this widget type -- a genuine contrast with Interactive Report/Cards, where region.ts documents ALL tested .call() actions being rejected with "Call not supported."
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Interactive Grids gallery app (Basic Editing page, page 30, static id "emp")
quirks.workaround: Use ApexInteractiveGridRegion (packages/testkit/src/components/interactive-grid.ts) for the confirmed methods. Do not call model/view/getRegion -- confirmed unsupported. Methods only observed as properties on getCurrentView()'s result (setSelectedRecords, getActiveRecordId, getContextRecord, gotoCell) are NOT yet individually verified -- treat them as unconfirmed until called directly and checked, the same discipline cards.ts applies to getRecords()/getModel().
quirks.status: confirmed, partial API surface verified

quirks.issue: CORRECTED -- this entry previously claimed apex.region(id).widget() returns null for chart regions, based on a single region ("area1") tested once. Re-tested live and found FALSE: it returns a real jQuery-wrapped element, exactly like Interactive Grid/Cards/Interactive Report, confirmed independently on THREE chart types (area1, stackCategoryChart, pie1). The real jQuery UI widget-factory plugin for Oracle JET charts, "ojChart", IS reachable through region.widget().ojChart(method) -- not a dead end requiring a raw jQuery selector, as the original entry claimed.
quirks.evidence: Live, method-by-method, on 3 independent chart types: apex.region('area1'/'stackCategoryChart'/'pie1').widget() all returned a real jQuery object (length 1, element id `<runtime id>_jet`), confirmed via explicit !== null checks each time -- and corroborated by the Sample Charts app's OWN exported JS code calling `apex.region("stackCategoryChart").widget().ojChart({...})` directly (p00009-bar.apx, a Dynamic Action's executeJsCode action). widget().ojChart('option') (no args) returned the full chart config object (25-42 keys depending on chart type: type/series/groups/xAxis/legend/styleDefaults/...). widget().ojChart('option', 'type') returned a single property ('area'/'pie' as expected). widget().ojChart('option', 'selectionMode', 'multiple') -- confirmed as a real, working SETTER via round-trip get-set-get, and the call returned the widget itself for chaining (standard widget-factory setter contract). getProperty/getOption remain confirmed NOT valid method names ("no such method" errors) -- 'option' is the real one.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Charts gallery app (Area page static id "area1"; Bar page static id "stackCategoryChart"; Pie page static id "pie1")
quirks.workaround: No longer needed -- use ApexChartRegion (packages/testkit/src/components/chart.ts), which graduated from a stub. `getOption()`/`getOption(key)`/`setOption(key, value)` all dispatch through the confirmed-working widget().ojChart('option', ...) path. `refresh()` remains on the inherited generic ApexRegion path, unchanged. A separate initialization-race quirk (see 'chart-widget-initialization-race' below) applies to timing, not to whether this API exists.
quirks.status: corrected; confirmed, working API surface verified

quirks.issue: JET chart widgets attach their `ojChart` jQuery UI widget-factory plugin ASYNCHRONOUSLY, after `page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` resolves. Calling ApexChartRegion.getOption()/setOption() (or any widget().ojChart(...) call) immediately after navigation can race this and throw "did not expose an ojChart() widget-factory method", even against a chart region confirmed to work moments later.
quirks.evidence: Live, reproduced in this project's own spike spec (spike/tests/chart-demo.spec.ts): calling ApexChartRegion.getOption('type') against 'pie1' right after `page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` + a page.title() check threw the widget-factory error; adding `page.waitForFunction(() => typeof apex.region('pie1')?.widget?.()?.ojChart === 'function')` before constructing the class resolved it deterministically across repeated runs. Interactive Grid's widget-factory calls (interactive-grid.ts) were NOT observed to race the same way in this project's testing, but have not been stress-tested for it either -- treat this as chart-specific until evidence says otherwise.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Charts gallery app (Pie page, static id "pie1")
quirks.workaround: Wait for the actual precondition before constructing ApexChartRegion or calling its methods: `await page.waitForFunction((id) => typeof (window as any).apex?.region?.(id)?.widget?.()?.ojChart === 'function', id)`. See spike/tests/chart-demo.spec.ts for the working pattern and ApexChartRegion's module doc for the same snippet.
quirks.status: confirmed, workaround verified

quirks.issue: The chart type declared in the .apx export (`chart { type: ... }`, typed as `ApexRegion.chartSettings.type`) does not always equal what the live JET widget reports via `ojChart('option', 'type')`. Found while auto-generating a Chart type-check assertion for @apx/testgen: a region declaring `chart { type: donut }` (sample-charts, region `donut-chart-sorting`, runtime id `donut1` via htmlDomId) reports `getOption('type') === 'pie'` live, NOT 'donut'. Root cause: Oracle JET's ojChart widget has no separate 'donut' type at all -- APEX's declarative 'donut' is JET's 'pie' type plus a nonzero `styleDefaults.pieInnerRadius`, confirmed present live. This is a real, deliberate APEX-level abstraction over a narrower JET type vocabulary, not a bug -- but it means asserting live-type-equals-declared-type broadly, across all 17 declared enum values, would be an unverified assumption, not a safe generalization.
quirks.evidence: Live: region 'donut-chart-sorting' declares `chart { type: donut }` in its .apx source (confirmed by direct grep of the raw export). Live: `apex.region('donut1').widget().ojChart('option', 'type')` returns 'pie', not 'donut'. Live: the same widget's full `option()` config has `styleDefaults.pieInnerRadius` truthy, confirming the donut visual is achieved via a pie-chart style property, not a distinct chart type. Separately confirmed NOT aliased: 'pie' (region 'pie-chart', runtime id 'pie1') and 'area' (region declaring `chart { type: area }` implicitly via omission default, runtime id 'area1') both report their declared type verbatim.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Charts gallery app (Pie page, static ids 'donut1' and 'pie1'; Area page, static id 'area1')
quirks.workaround: @apx/testgen's auto-generated Chart assertion checks that the live type resolves to a real, non-empty string (proves the widget wired up correctly) -- it does NOT assert equality against the declared chartSettings.type, specifically because of this finding. If you need to assert a SPECIFIC declared type live, confirm the mapping for that exact type value first (only 'pie' and 'area' are confirmed direct matches so far; 'donut' is confirmed to map to 'pie'; the other 14 enum values -- boxPlot, bubble, combination, statusMeterGauge, funnel, gantt, line, lineWithArea, polar, pyramid, radar, range, scatter, stock -- are unconfirmed either way).
quirks.status: confirmed for one alias (donut->pie) and two direct matches (pie, area); the remaining 14 declared type values are unconfirmed

quirks.component: Page items -- 'required' visual marker vs. real server-side enforcement (data-entry-simple-form page, UX Pattern Catalog)
quirks.issue: The red required-field marker on this reference-pattern page (Name, Job Code items) is decorative only -- it is NOT backed by a real declarative Validation or 'Value Required' server-side check. Submitting the page with both fields empty performs a genuine POST to wwv_flow.accept (a real server round trip, not a client-side block) but #APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE and every per-item _error_placeholder element stay empty and class u-hidden -- no validation ever fires.
quirks.evidence: Live: clicked the page's 'Primary Action' (Save) button 3 times with P410_NAME and P410_JOB empty. Network log showed 3 distinct 'POST .../ords/wwv_flow.accept?p_context=ux-pattern-catalog/data-entry-simple-form/...' -> 200 OK each time (confirmed via read_network_requests, so this is a real submission, not a client-side no-op). After every submission: document.getElementById('APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE').className stayed 'apex-page-error u-hidden', innerHTML stayed ''; all 8 *_error_placeholder elements (P410_NAME_error_placeholder, P410_JOB_error_placeholder, etc., class 'a-Form-error') stayed present but empty. No console errors, no apex.message calls observed.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (data-entry-simple-form page, page 410) -- the only one of this project's real live-accessible APEX apps reachable without login (public authentication scheme)
quirks.workaround: None needed for testkit purposes, but a real finding: do not assume a 'required' visual marker on this specific catalog page implies a real, testable server-side validation. This page is illustrative of the required-marker UI pattern only, not a functioning validation round trip. Use a different page/app (one with a real declarative Validation, e.g. Sample Interactive Grids page 31 'Validation') to exercise and assert on a genuine validation-failure display.
quirks.status: confirmed live -- this specific page has no functioning server-side validation to observe, despite the required-field visual marker

quirks.issue: Search box and column-header sort ARE reliably drivable through the visible UI via Playwright accessible-role locators, distinct from the already-confirmed-private JS widget API (see 'interactive-report-private-methods') -- but with two real behavioral quirks that must be handled explicitly, not assumed away: (1) an unquoted multi-word search term matches ANY word (OR), not the whole phrase; (2) clicking a column header's sort-trigger link fails Playwright's default actionability check every time, because APEX's own stickyTableHeader widget renders an always-present, absolutely-positioned visual clone of the header row directly on top of the real one, at a higher z-index, from the moment the page loads (no scrolling needed to reproduce).
quirks.evidence: Confirmed via real Playwright automation (not just the browser MCP pane) against UX Pattern Catalog's browse-interactive-report page. Search: getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Row Search' }).fill('Item 2') + press('Enter') fired a real QUICK_FILTER AJAX action (confirmed via page.waitForResponse and a genuine apexbeforerefresh/apexafterrefresh event pair on the region's own DOM element) but returned all 48 rows unfiltered, because the word 'Item' alone appears in every row's title; the SAME search with the term quoted ('"Item 2"') correctly narrowed to 11 rows (Item 2, Item 20-29). Sort: a plain headerLink.click() on the Category, Title, and Priority column headers timed out 3/3 times with Playwright reporting '<a> from <div id="stickyTableHeader_1" class="...js-stickyTableHeader..."> subtree intercepts pointer events'; page.evaluate() confirmed the sticky clone's getBoundingClientRect() exactly overlaps the real <th> (same x/y/width/height) with display:block/visibility:visible/position:absolute/zIndex:300 immediately after navigation, no scroll performed. Force-clicking the REAL header link ({ force: true }) reliably opened the sort menu and updated aria-sort on the real <th> to 'ascending'/'descending' as expected, confirmed on 3 independent columns, each checked twice (ascending then descending).
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (browse-interactive-report page), region id R11643575732369775 (no advanced { htmlDomId } override; export identifier is 'interactive-report', a different string -- read off the live DOM, not derivable from the export)
quirks.workaround: Use searchInteractiveReport()/sortReportColumn()/getColumnSortState() from interactive-report.ts. searchInteractiveReport() does not auto-quote -- callers wanting exact-phrase matching must pass the quotes themselves. sortReportColumn() always force-clicks the header link and documents why.
quirks.status: confirmed live, working, shipped

quirks.issue: A classicReport column's <th> DOM id equals the .apx column's identifier verbatim, with no override field needed (an even stronger, column-level extension of ADR-003's region-level htmlDomId finding) -- but a plain '#identifier' locator hits a Playwright strict-mode violation, because APEX's stickyTableHeader widget duplicates the SAME id onto its own clone <th>, unlike Interactive Report's sticky clone (which uses a structurally different, non-accessible-role container and does not collide on id).
quirks.evidence: Cross-checked live DOM against the real .apx export (item-detail-full page, child-records region): the export declares 'column CHILD_RECORD_NAME ( ... )' / 'column CHILD_RECORD_TYPE ( ... )' / 'column OWNER_NAME ( ... )' / 'column CHILD_RECORD_STATUS ( ... )' / 'column DUE_DATE ( ... )'; the live DOM has <th id="CHILD_RECORD_NAME">, <th id="CHILD_RECORD_TYPE">, etc., matching exactly, for all 5 columns. Separately confirmed via document.querySelectorAll('#CHILD_RECORD_NAME') that TWO elements share this id: one inside table#report_table_R6216196640130009_orig (the real table) and one inside table#report_table_R6216196640130009 (the sticky clone, class t-fht-thead js-stickyTableHeader), both reporting offsetParent !== null (visible). Scoping to table[id$="_orig"] #CHILD_RECORD_NAME resolved to exactly 1 element with the correct text. Also confirmed classicReport columns carry no sort affordance at all (no wrapping <a>, no aria-sort attribute) -- a real, structural difference from Interactive Report, not a gap.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (item-detail-full page, child-records region, classicReport type)
quirks.workaround: Use classicReportColumnById() from report-column.ts, which scopes to table[id$="_orig"] to avoid the sticky-clone duplicate. Use reportColumnHeader() (accessible-role locator) for presence/label assertions instead -- it is NOT affected by the duplicate-id issue, since the sticky clone is not exposed via the accessibility tree.
quirks.status: confirmed live, working (with the documented scoping fix), shipped

quirks.issue: Unlike classicReport (see 'classic-report-column-id-verbatim'), an Interactive Report column's <th> DOM id is an APEX-internal auto-generated numeric id with no corresponding field anywhere in the static .apx export -- genuinely undiscoverable from export data alone, the same 'layer 3' class of finding ADR-003 already established for regions without htmlDomId.
quirks.evidence: Cross-checked live DOM against the real .apx export (browse-interactive-report page): export column identifiers are TITLE/CATEGORY/PRIORITY/FLAG_1..4/UPDATED_ON/etc.; live DOM ids are C11643982695369779/C11644187233369781/C11644419072369784/etc. -- no relationship. Confirmed document.getElementById('TITLE') (the export identifier) resolves to nothing; the real id only discoverable live, e.g. via getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Title' }).getAttribute('id').
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (browse-interactive-report page, interactive-report region)
quirks.workaround: Use reportColumnHeader()/reportColumnHeadersPresent() (accessible-role locators keyed by heading TEXT, not id) for Interactive Report columns -- never attempt to construct the DOM id from .apx data for this region type.
quirks.status: confirmed live, genuinely undiscoverable from static data -- not a parser gap

quirks.issue: A Cards region's row action (action-d) IS reachable via an accessible link role with the action's label as its accessible name -- but (1) the label is NOT unique per region, repeating once per rendered record, with no confirmed way to scope to a specific record from .apx metadata alone; and (2) on the only live app available, every tested row action (Cards 'Edit' link, a Cards title link, List's 'Row Action 1/2/3' menu items) is a non-functional placeholder -- href="#" or no href, zero network requests, zero URL change, zero console activity on click.
quirks.evidence: faceted-search-cards: page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Edit', exact: true }) resolved to 24 elements (one per card); clicking .first() produced no URL change, no wwv_flow.* network request, no console output. The card title link ('Item 1', href="#") behaved identically. faceted-search-content-row (List/action-e): row actions are NOT rendered as direct same-labeled links -- each row instead has ONE 'Row Actions' button (itself non-unique, 15 instances) that opens a menu whose menuitem-role entries ('Row Action 1'/'2'/'3') are the actual actions; clicking one produced the same zero-effect result. Contrast checked on the SAME app: Interactive Report's structurally similar 'Primary Row Action' link (48 instances, also non-unique) DOES have a real href and DOES navigate (confirmed: URL changed to a real, if broken, target page) -- so click-driven navigation via a row action is not impossible in principle, just unverified for the Cards/List family specifically.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (faceted-search-cards and faceted-search-content-row pages)
quirks.workaround: Use regionActionLocator()/expectRegionActionPresent() for presence-only assertions (matching, checkable, count-tolerant). Do NOT assert click-through effects (navigation/dialog/DOM change) for this component family -- no verified, working example exists yet on any live app this project has access to. List/action-e's menu-based rendering is a confirmed-different DOM contract, deliberately not wrapped in this pass.
quirks.status: presence confirmed live and shipped; click-effect verification confirmed BLOCKED (dead links on the only live app available, not a testkit gap)

quirks.issue: The official EBNF confirms button.advanced.htmlDomId/staticId exist (button-advanced-property production) -- the SAME advanced-group mechanism already confirmed for regions (ADR-003) -- but no button anywhere in this project's local corpus (46+ real exports, including a full grep of every page of UX Pattern Catalog, the app used for the live check below) has ever been found to set either field. When absent, the runtime DOM id is an APEX-internal auto-generated id of the form B<numeric>, structurally identical to region's R<numeric> fallback, with no corresponding field anywhere in the static export -- genuinely undiscoverable from export data alone, the button-level analog of 'region-id-not-static-id'.
quirks.evidence: grep -rn "staticId" across the full local UX Pattern Catalog export (46+ pages): zero occurrences anywhere. grep -rn "htmlDomId" found exactly 3 occurrences project-wide, all three on regions (active-facets, primary_items_list), none on a button. Live: document ids for 'Primary Action' buttons on 3 different pages (browse-interactive-report, faceted-search-cards, data-entry-simple-form) were B9441596513426189/B9407603832418760/B6286693148755797 -- all match /^B\d+$/, none related to the button's .apx identifier (primary-action) or buttonName (PRIMARY_ACTION).
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (browse-interactive-report, faceted-search-cards, data-entry-simple-form pages); full local export grepped for the field's absence
quirks.workaround: None needed for button.ts's existing behavior -- it already uses accessible-role/label locators (buttonByLabel), which do not depend on the DOM id at all. ApexButton.htmlDomId is typed now so a future button that DOES set a custom Static ID is captured and diffable; do not build a htmlDomId-based button locator until a real button that sets one exists to verify the resolution convention against (ADR-002).
quirks.status: confirmed live and via full-corpus static grep -- genuinely undiscoverable/unset in every real button seen so far, not a parser gap

quirks.issue: A report column's declared `heading.heading` is NOT a reliable predictor of whether it renders its own `columnheader`-role <th> on Interactive Report -- confirmed live, a real counter-example on the SAME app/page already used as this pass's positive ground truth. This blocked an attempted generator auto-assertion (see workaround) that would otherwise have silently shipped a test guaranteed to fail on real data.
quirks.evidence: browse-interactive-report declares 14 columns with a heading, but only 9 real `columnheader`-role elements exist at runtime: BADGE_STATE/META/OVERLINE are `type: hidden` (expected, no header -- consistent with classicReport's rule) but DESCRIPTION (`type: plainText`, NOT hidden) and ICON (`type: themeTemplateComponent/avatar`, NOT hidden) ALSO have zero matching `columnheader` elements (confirmed via page.getByRole('columnheader', { name, exact: true }).count() === 0 for both) -- their content is instead folded into the 'Title' column's own cell (icon + title + secondary text rendered together, visible directly in the live report), a real Interactive Report 'primary column group' rendering pattern with no equivalent in classicReport's simpler per-column <th> model.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (browse-interactive-report page, interactive-report region)
quirks.workaround: Do NOT auto-generate expectReportColumnHeadersPresent() from the full list of a region's declared column headings for interactiveReport -- an attempt to do exactly this in packages/generator/src/lib.ts was built, caught by this live counter-example before being committed, and reverted. reportColumnHeader()/expectReportColumnHeadersPresent() remain real, verified, SHIP-WORTHY capabilities for a caller who supplies a deliberately curated, live-confirmed list of headings (as spike/tests/report-column-demo.spec.ts and interactive-report-demo.spec.ts do) -- the gap is specifically in auto-deriving that list from static .apx metadata alone for Interactive Report. classicReport did not exhibit this problem in the one region checked (5/5 non-hidden columns had their own <th>, exact match) but was not re-tested broadly enough to auto-wire either, out of caution given this exact class of finding.
quirks.status: confirmed live -- real gap, generator auto-wiring correctly NOT shipped

quirks.component: Interactive Grid validation failures -- messages.ts expectError() coverage (Sample Interactive Grids page 31, 'Validation')
quirks.issue: Resolves the previously-inconclusive question from docs/ecosystem-roadmap.md's Seventh round follow-up (2026-07-27/28): does a real, server-side Interactive Grid validation() failure surface through messages.ts's expectError() (#APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE toggled u-visible), zero new runtime code needed? ANSWER: it depends on the validation TYPE -- two genuinely different mechanisms, not one. (1) Page-level SQL row/column validation() components (comm-limit, hire-date-in-past) DO go through a real AJAX round trip (wwv_flow.ajax, interactiveGridAutoRowProcessing); the JSON response's errors array carries location:['page','inline'], apex.message.showErrors() IS called with those exact error objects, and #APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE DOES toggle to u-visible with the literal configured error text -- expectError() already covers this, confirmed with zero new code. (2) Column-level valueRequired:true (ENAME/HIREDATE) is a CLIENT-SIDE-only check, exactly as the page's own help text says ('Required is the only validation done on the client by default'): clicking Save with a required cell empty NEVER issues an AJAX request at all (confirmed zero POSTs to wwv_flow.ajax), and instead calls apex.message.alert('Correct errors before saving.') -- a real, different, documented apex.message API (a modal dialog, role=alertdialog, Universal Theme's ui-dialog--notification), marking the offending <td role=gridcell> with class is-error. #APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE stays u-hidden throughout -- expectError() does NOT catch this case; it needed a new helper.
quirks.evidence: Live, reproduced twice each for both mechanisms (never generalized from one instance, per this project's own Chart widget() precedent): (1) comm-limit -- edited KING (empno 7839, SAL=5000) Commission to 10000 (violates COMM < 1.5*SAL); wwv_flow.ajax POST response body: {"errors":[{"message":"Commission must be less than 1.5 times the Salary","unsafe":false,"location":["page","inline"],"regionDomId":"emp","recordId":"7839"}]}; a monkey-patched apex.message.showErrors captured the identical array; document.getElementById('APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE').className became 'apex-page-error u-visible', textContent 'Error Message ... 1 error has occurredCommission must be less than 1.5 times the Salary'. Also confirmed for hire-date-in-past (message 'Hire Date must be in the past.', same location/showErrors/u-visible pattern), though only reproducible combined with a null-Hire-Date valueRequired failure on a newly-added row (to_date(null) < SYSDATE is NULL in Oracle SQL, not TRUE, so both validations correctly fire together -- the inline show:inline date-picker's Year <select> is a fixed +/-10 window around the field's CURRENT value, not around today, so an isolated future-date reproduction is not scriptable on an existing row). A rejected AJAX row-save is never persisted -- confirmed by reloading and finding COMM back to null ('-', this app's showNullValuesAs). (2) valueRequired -- cleared CLARK's (empno 7782) Name cell and clicked Save: a page.on('request') listener recorded zero POSTs to wwv_flow.ajax; a monkey-patched apex.message.alert captured exactly ['Correct errors before saving.']; #APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE.className stayed 'apex-page-error u-hidden'; the Name <td role=gridcell> gained class is-error; a real role=alertdialog element appeared (class 'ui-dialog ui-dialog--notification ui-dialog--modern ...') with one button, accessible name 'OK'. Nothing was ever sent to the server, so nothing persisted -- confirmed by reloading (after accepting the resulting beforeunload prompt for the unsaved client edit) and finding Name back to 'CLARK'.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: Sample Interactive Grids gallery app (Validation page, page 31, static id "emp") -- both comm-limit and valueRequired confirmed live twice each; hire-date-in-past confirmed live twice, combined with valueRequired on a new row
quirks.workaround: Use expectError() (packages/testkit/src/components/messages.ts) for page-level SQL validation() failures on an Interactive Grid, exactly as for a classic Form region -- no IG-specific code needed. Use the new expectAlert()/dismissAlert()/alertDialog() helpers (same file, added this pass) for column-level valueRequired failures instead -- these query role=alertdialog, not #APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE. Do not assume one mechanism covers all Interactive Grid validation types.
quirks.status: confirmed live -- resolved (was 'inconclusive, blocked on login' in the prior pass; credentials became available and the reproduction completed)
quirks.source: packages/testkit/src/components/messages.ts, spike/tests/interactive-grid-validation-demo.spec.ts, docs/ecosystem-roadmap.md Seventh round follow-up (corrected in place)

quirks.component: CRUD test generation discovery pass (GitHub issue #5) -- primary-key detection and save/delete-button identification convention over a real form-over-table page
quirks.issue: Before any CRUD generation code (create -> verify(self-created value) -> edit -> verify -> delete -> verify) could be scoped, this pass needed to confirm live, against a real form-over-table page: (a) reliable primary-key detection from the typed AST/export, and (b) a reliable save/delete-button identification convention. Neither could be positively confirmed end-to-end in this environment -- (a) is a real, confirmed AST gap, not just an access gap; (b)'s button-location half is reconfirmed but the 'does clicking Save produce a real, observable, self-consistent persisted value' half could not be verified anywhere reachable.
quirks.evidence: PRIMARY KEY: `region.source.tableName` (ApexRegion.source.tableName, packages/parser/src/ast.ts:78) is a real, always-attempted typed field -- confirmed present in the parser. But there is NO typed PK column/PK item field anywhere in the AST for a region: the only place a PK ever appears is `process.target { tableName, pkColumn, pkItem, returnKeyIntoItem }` on an `autoRowProcessing`/`formAutoRowProcessing` process, and per ast.ts:522-541 this `target` group is DELIBERATELY left untyped (kept in `raw` only, cross-referenced against the official EBNF which has no `target` group at all in the `process` production -- a confirmed real EBNF gap, not a parser oversight). A generator would have to scan `page.processes` for `type` in {autoRowProcessing, formAutoRowProcessing} and read `raw['target.pkColumn']`/`raw['target.pkItem']` directly -- an ad hoc raw-bag read across a DIFFERENT AST node (process) than the one holding the table name (region), not a clean, single, typed contract. SAVE/DELETE BUTTON IDENTIFICATION: reconfirmed live against UX Pattern Catalog's 'Data Entry - Simple Form' page (data-entry-simple-form, page 410, no login required) -- the 'Primary Action' (Save) button resolves via `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Primary Action', exact: true })` to the SAME runtime id already on record from the Eighth round (`B6286693148755797`), stable across sessions -- button.ts's accessible-role/label strategy (per the already-confirmed `button-id-not-static-id` dead end above) holds for a Save-labeled action specifically, not just presence checks. NOT confirmed: a Delete button on any reachable page in this app -- none of the 9 leaf pages (data-entry-simple-form, data-entry-drawer-form, item-detail-summary, item-detail-full, item-selection-with-details, browse-interactive-report, faceted-search-cards, faceted-search-content-row, dashboards) expose a Delete action at all. ROUND-TRIP PERSISTENCE (the actual thing a CRUD test needs): confirmed NOT client-observable on this app, though the exact mechanism took two passes to characterize correctly -- an in-place correction, not a silent one. First pass (manual, via a raw DOM `.click()` through a browser-automation tool, checking `location.href` in a SEPARATE subsequent call): concluded no navigation occurred at all. That was WRONG, caught by the live spike spec (`spike/tests/crud-generation-discovery-demo.spec.ts`) using a real Playwright click, which failed immediately with 'Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation' -- proof a real navigation does happen and the manual check's second, separate read simply ran after the page had already reloaded out from under it. CORRECTED finding, confirmed twice via `page.on('framenavigated')` plus `page.waitForNavigation()`: clicking 'Primary Action' triggers a REAL full-page POST-redirect-GET (`wwv_flow.accept` -> 200 OK -> a genuine browser navigation), not an AJAX-only partial-page-refresh -- exactly one `framenavigated` event fires, and it redirects back to the IDENTICAL page URL (a 'create another' pattern, not a redirect to a new saved-record URL). What's unchanged by the correction: on the reloaded page, `apex.item('P410_NAME').getValue()` is blank again (not echoing the value this test itself supplied), the hidden `P410_ID` item (present in the DOM, the standard APEX form-region PK-item naming convention) is still blank (not switched into 'edit the record you just created' mode), and `#APEX_SUCCESS_MESSAGE`/`#APEX_ERROR_MESSAGE` both stay `u-hidden`. This means the real blocker is narrower than 'nothing happens' -- it's specifically that NOTHING CLIENT-OBSERVABLE distinguishes 'a row was actually inserted server-side with no visible confirmation' from 'nothing was inserted at all'; a self-created-data assertion needs to observe a value round-trip, and there is nothing here to observe either way. Separately, the report-to-detail navigation path was checked as an alternate CRUD entry point: every 'Primary Row Action' link on `browse-interactive-report` points to the IDENTICAL url `.../ux-pattern-catalog/7?session=...` regardless of which row it's attached to (no per-record id in the href at all), and that url itself resolves to a live 'Not Found' page (confirmed via `page.request.get()`, HTTP 404) -- a dead link, not a working master-detail edit target. This is consistent with, and extends, this project's own already-recorded finding that click-through effects on this specific app are 'a confirmed dead end... decorative, non-functional demo affordances' (see `region-action-cards-not-unique-inert` above) -- the same pattern applies to this page's Save action and to the IR's row-action link, not just to Cards/List row actions. `APX_LOGIN_TEST_USERNAME`/`APX_LOGIN_TEST_PASSWORD` were checked (`env | grep APX_LOGIN_TEST`) and confirmed UNSET in this environment, so Sample Interactive Grids / Sample Charts -- the apps this project's own roadmap and prior rounds identify as having genuine credentialed CRUD-shaped pages -- were not reachable to attempt the same test against a page that might behave differently.
quirks.reproducedAgainst: UX Pattern Catalog app (data-entry-simple-form page 410, live 'Primary Action' click via a real Playwright click, run twice, 4/4 assertions passing both times; browse-interactive-report page, live row-action href inspection + a real HTTP request confirming the 404; all 9 leaf pages under Dashboards/Browse and Search/Item Details/Data Entry checked for a Delete action) -- the only live app reachable without login in this environment. Sample Interactive Grids / Sample Charts NOT reached -- credentials unset.
quirks.workaround: No generation code was built on the strength of this pass -- see docs/ecosystem-roadmap.md's Ninth round follow-up for the full discovery writeup and the deferred build plan. Two independent things would need to be true before CRUD generation could proceed with confidence: (1) a typed `pkColumn`/`pkItem` field surfaced from a page's `autoRowProcessing`/`formAutoRowProcessing` process target (a parser task, not a runtime one -- `/parser` owns this), reachable without an ad hoc raw-bag cross-reference between two different AST node types; (2) a real, reachable, credentialed form-over-table page (Sample Interactive Grids' underlying EMP form, or equivalent) to actually observe a create -> PK assigned -> read-back round trip, since UX Pattern Catalog's own form pages are confirmed non-functional for this purpose specifically. Re-run this discovery pass the moment either credentials become available or a new live app with a genuine, working single-record form surfaces.
quirks.status: blocked -- not a design rejection, an evidence gap (AST: real gap, confirmed; live app: dead-end confirmed on the no-login app; credentialed apps: access-blocked, not yet attempted)
